title: Piorun SAFE contracting develops into a reported multilateral allied procurement route
source_unit: Polish and Lithuanian defense-ministry/government Piorun procurement announcements
geography: Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, Norway, and Estonia; NATO/EU defense procurement

reported_piorun_scope.value: several thousand Piorun systems with simulators, training, and logistics packages

polish_force_share.unit: percent or more of sets stated as intended for Polish Armed Forces

safe_common_procurement_route.value: joint procurement under the EU SAFE program for Poland and other NATO states

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official Polish Ministry of National Defence announcement. Framework value, product scope, named users, intended Polish share, and financing route are retained as reported agreement-stage measures.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not provide country-by-country quantities, executive orders, payment schedules, delivery dates, acceptance, or operational availability. Framework scope is not delivered inventory.
observations.subgroup: Mesko Piorun production and allied common-procurement route under SAFE.
observations.counterinterpretation: A multilateral framework can signal shared demand and supplier influence while leaving actual orders, financing drawdown, delivery, and dependence on foreign inputs unresolved.

observations.period: 2026-09-11; first executive contract and reported external procurement response

denominator.unit: first executive contract under the reported Piorun framework

external_buyers_reported.unit: countries reported by the Prime Minister's Office as buyers

market_response_stage.value: Piorun described as an important Polish export product with allied procurement decisions

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official Polish Prime Minister's Office update. The first executive contract is separated from the framework, and reported allied purchase decisions are treated as an external-demand signal rather than delivered export volume.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not report quantities by foreign country, delivery or acceptance, revenue, export authorization, or operational use. It does not independently establish that SAFE caused each foreign procurement decision.
observations.subgroup: Polish Armament Agency, Mesko, and allied Piorun procurement route at MSPO 2026.
observations.counterinterpretation: A public announcement of allied purchasing can reflect a framework or political commitment that later changes, and may strengthen Polish export positioning without proving durable bargaining power or production independence.

observations.period: 2026-08-24; MESKO framework scale and delivery horizon

denominator.unit: MESKO account of the EDIRPA VSHORAD framework agreement

planned_framework_value.unit: Polish zloty net; planned value of executive contracts reported by MESKO

planned_delivery_horizon.unit: calendar year; reported end of delivery horizon

polish_force_share.unit: percent or more of missiles and launchers stated as intended for Polish Armed Forces

observations.method: Bounded extraction from MESKO's official company account of the 2026-08-24 EDIRPA VSHORAD framework. The source adds quantity classes and a delivery horizon to the government-reported framework, but remains a company-reported agreement-stage account.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not provide country-by-country quantities, lot dates, payment or obligation schedules, acceptance criteria, completed deliveries, or the SAFE-funded incremental production actually assigned to this framework. Several thousand and several hundred are intentionally retained as quantity classes rather than converted to point estimates.
observations.subgroup: MESKO/PGZ EDIRPA VSHORAD framework for Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, and Norway.
observations.counterinterpretation: A stated 2030 horizon can indicate a long implementation runway without proving that contracts will be fully exercised, delivered on schedule, accepted, or operationally available.

earlier_annual_capacity.unit: Piorun missiles per year; reported earlier capability

current_annual_capacity.unit: Piorun missiles per year; reported current capability

ambition_annual_capacity.unit: Piorun missiles per year; reported ambition is above this level

capacity_multiplier_claim.unit: reported approximate multiple from earlier to current capacity

observations.method: Bounded extraction from MESKO's official company account. Capacity statements are retained as reported industrial context and are not treated as independently audited output, plant throughput, or SAFE-attributable production.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not define the earlier and current measurement windows, plant boundary, product configuration, utilization rate, critical-input constraints, accepted output, or allocation across Polish and foreign customers. The ambition above 2,000 is a target, not realized capacity.
observations.subgroup: MESKO/PGZ Piorun production capacity in the Polish defense-industrial base.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher stated capacity may improve the ability to absorb demand while leaving bottlenecks, input dependence, delivery sequencing, and effective customer access unresolved.

observations.period: 2023-12-12; MESKO archive-listed first Norway batch handover

reported_norway_scope.value: several hundred Piorun missiles and launchers

contract_timing.value: contract signed in Oslo approximately one year before the page's stated handover

safe_edripa_link.value: not identified; handover predates the 2026 SAFE/EDIRPA framework

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official MESKO archive and linked company page. The archive dates the first Norway handover to 2023-12-12; the notice reports several hundred missiles and launchers and a contract signed in Oslo approximately one year earlier. This is kept as a separately scoped export-delivery observation rather than pooled with the 2026 SAFE route.
observations.uncertainty: The sources do not give an exact contract date, contract identifier, exact quantity, acceptance record, payment status, or operational-use evidence. The 2023 date is the archive-listed handover/publication date; the underlying notice does not independently specify a handover timestamp.
observations.subgroup: Norwegian Piorun export route separate from the 2026 Poland-led SAFE/EDIRPA framework unless a contract match is later documented.
observations.counterinterpretation: A reported first-batch handover demonstrates an export-delivery stage for Norway but does not demonstrate SAFE execution, general delivery performance, increased production, or reduced allied dependence.

observations.period: 2026-01-16 and 2026-09-09; Lithuanian procurement and supply-chain confirmation

denominator.unit: two Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence records concerning Piorun acquisition and Poland-Lithuania supply-chain cooperation

lithuanian_side_value.unit: euros; approximate Lithuanian-side deal value reported January 2026

lithuanian_acquisition_status.value: Lithuania described itself as purchasing Piorun with Poland, Estonia, and Norway and later discussed acquisition progress with Poland

supply_chain_integration_action.value: Lithuania and Poland discussed defense-industry supply-chain participation and signed a separate semiconductor/PCO cooperation agreement at MSPO

observations.method: Non-pooled extraction from two Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence records. The January procurement statement and September follow-up are retained as separate external-action stages and are not treated as delivery evidence.
observations.uncertainty: The Lithuanian records do not provide Piorun delivery or acceptance dates, country-specific quantities, full contract identifiers, or evidence that the supply-chain cooperation agreement is part of the Piorun contract. The reported EUR amount is a Lithuanian-side deal estimate.
observations.subgroup: Lithuanian defense procurement and Poland-Lithuania industrial cooperation linked to the Piorun route.
observations.counterinterpretation: External participation can widen demand and supply-chain ties without reducing dependence on Polish or non-Polish components, and a procurement-stage commitment is not realized capability.

observations.period: 2026-06-23; official Lithuanian inventory/planning update and SAFE-route delivery recheck through 2026-09-18

denominator.unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence Piorun planning statement and bounded official-source recheck

planned_purchase_status.value: Piorun acquisition described as planned for the year

safe_route_delivery_notice_found.unit: bounded search for a country-level Piorun handover, acceptance, or operational-use notice attributable to the 2026 SAFE/EDIRPA route through 2026-09-18

observations.method: Bounded reading of the official Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence inventory update, followed by a targeted official-source recheck for country-level Piorun delivery, acceptance, or operational-use notices attributable to the 2026 SAFE/EDIRPA route. A separate 2023 MESKO report of a Norway handover is retained separately and does not invalidate this route-specific non-observation.
observations.uncertainty: Search coverage is limited to the official-source route checked and cannot exclude a private, classified, differently named, or unindexed event. The planning statement does not identify a contract, quantity, payment, delivery lot, or acceptance record; the separate Norway page is dated 2023 but not linked to SAFE/EDIRPA.
observations.subgroup: Lithuanian Piorun acquisition route within the wider Poland-led SAFE/common-procurement pathway.
observations.counterinterpretation: A planned purchase can coexist with a signed framework or later negotiation progress; absence of a located SAFE-attributable public handover notice does not establish absence of delivery, and a separate pre- or non-SAFE export handover cannot be pooled into SAFE performance.

denominator.unit: Piorun systems reported as having left the Mesko production line by the three-thousandth unit milestone

piorun_production_milestone.unit: systems; reported three-thousandth unit produced in 2024

safe_attribution.value: not attributed to the 2026 SAFE framework

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official Polish Ministry of State Assets report about Mesko. The three-thousandth-unit milestone is retained as a historical product-level production baseline and is not treated as a 2026 SAFE output measure.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not provide annual production series, delivery/acceptance records, customer allocation, export quantities, or a plant-level output denominator. A cumulative milestone cannot be converted into a production rate or SAFE incremental quantity.
observations.subgroup: Mesko Piorun production before the 2026 SAFE framework and multilateral procurement route.
observations.counterinterpretation: Existing production demonstrates prior industrial capability but does not establish that the later SAFE framework was unnecessary, that capacity can meet the new scope, or that Poland controls all critical inputs and technology.

related_sources.claim: Normalized note preserves the framework, executive-contract, allied procurement, and non-delivery boundaries.
The SAFE contracting record supplies the broader Polish legislative and domestic-industry allocation stage.
MON supplies the Piorun SAFE framework, scope, value, and named allied-user route.
The Prime Minister's Office supplies the first executive-contract and reported allied procurement response.
Lithuanian MoD supplies external procurement-stage corroboration and an approximate Lithuanian-side value.
MESKO supplies the reported quantity classes, delivery horizon, and production-capacity context for the Piorun EDIRPA/SAFE framework.
MESKO reports the first Norway batch handover and describes the separate bilateral contract scope.
MESKO's archive dates the Norway first-batch handover to 2023-12-12.

boundary: This record advances the domestic SAFE contracting -> allied procurement and market-response arrow. It does not establish delivered Piorun quantities, acceptance, readiness, battlefield use, export revenue, supplier replaceability, or a causal effect of SAFE on foreign procurement decisions.
